assessment: The incumbent reliably delivered the ordered designs in the previous batch, while its reference-table check caught seven fit problems before dispatch. Rework clustered in large covers (5/8), versus medium (2/14) and small (0/18), supporting investigation of size-dependent dimensional error without establishing its cause. Small unadjusted covers demonstrate feasible individual times below 32 minutes, but do not establish the incoming batch median. A concrete limit is the two observed customer failures on rounded tables: reference-table success may miss customer geometry. Length shrinkage is observed; its contribution to fitting failures and width behavior remain unknown. Estimated waste by weight does not establish the area constraint.

openings.claim: The common allowance may produce a size-dependent dimensional mismatch that contributes to larger-cover rework.
openings.delta: Distinguish an unsuitable cutting target from cutting or sewing variation before applying revised allowances across the stock.
openings.prediction: If the allowance is responsible, accurately cut and sewn panels will still show consistent size-dependent fit residuals on reference tables; irregular residuals associated with operator or cutting direction would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Sequence initial small, medium and large orders through fitting before cutting the remainder. Record card targets, actual cut and finished dimensions, design, direction, operator, adjustment and total working time. Check retained offcuts in both directions through the stipulated wash test. Evaluate any allowance change against planned and actual cutting waste by area.
assumptions: Initial covers remain deliverable in their ordered sizes and designs.
Measurement and sequencing fit the three-week window and 350-unit budget.
Allowance changes require evidence; wash durability must still pass.

openings.claim: Do nominal dimensions and unrepresented corner geometry independently explain customer fit failures after reference-table acceptance?
openings.delta: Test transfer from reference tables to customers' actual tables, separately from production dimensional error.
openings.prediction: A geometry mismatch would produce local corner interference despite matching overall dimensions; a nominal-dimension mismatch would appear in measured length or width.
openings.probe: Use the six willing customers to obtain actual dimensions and corner profiles, prioritizing the four nominal-only orders where possible. Compare with reference geometry and observe first placement on represented customer tables without coaching adjustment.
assumptions: Customers include relevant incoming orders or comparable tables.
Measurements arrive before their panels are cut.
Any subsequent adaptation preserves ordered design, removability, wash performance and cutting limits.
